scope: Theorem 7.11 (Decompletion, with profinite parameters) of the manuscript “Failure of finite assembly for a chromatic overlap at the prime three” (preprints/Failure-of-finite-assembly-for-a-chromatic-overlap-at-the-prime-three-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 318 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b1e58a49eb364dd8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 48. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every compact profinite space T, the natural coefficient inclusions induce a quasi-isomorphism C• cts(H, R; T) = colim U,e C• cts(H, (LU )1/pe ; T) −→ colim U C• cts(H, (LU )♭ ; T). (7.22) It is natural in T, in marking-stage inclusions, and for the P- and J-actions. In particular, Ha C• cts(H, R; T) = ⎧ ⎪ ⎪ ⎨ ⎪ ⎪ ⎩ Ccts(T, k), a = 0, Ccts(T, ℓ), a = 3, 0, a ̸= 0, 3. (7.23) The two lines are discrete. The residual P/H-action on them is trivial, J acts trivially on k, and O× F ⊂ J acts on ℓ by δ.
